# Halt

> Halt (haltmode.com, also called Halt Mode) is a website and app blocker for Windows. It blocks distracting websites in every browser on the PC, closes blocked apps and games, gives sites and apps a daily time limit, and has an adult content filter for the whole PC. You choose a lock that decides how hard it is to stop early. Halt Basic is free; Halt Pro is $29, paid once, with no subscription and no account. Buy it once and it is yours for good, with every update included. Halt will never be sold as a subscription.

Status: available now. Download: https://haltmode.com/download/ . Buy Halt Pro: https://haltmode.com/#pricing . Terms and refunds: https://haltmode.com/terms/
Demo video (40 seconds): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dLh6RvI-_Ho

## What Halt does

- Blocks websites in Chrome, Edge, Brave and Firefox, private windows included, through the browsers' own policy settings (the ones schools and companies use), so there is no extension to switch off.
- Blocks part of a site, such as one page, a YouTube channel or a playlist, and keeps the rest open.
- Closes blocked apps and games, including Steam, Epic and Riot games, within 2 seconds, with a short message.
- Daily time limits for sites, apps and bundles, for example YouTube 2 hours a day. A site counts while it is the tab in front; an app counts while it is in front or playing sound. Limits reset at midnight.
- Five locks for stopping a session early: a timer (no way out), a wait, typing a long random text, a restart, or a password someone else keeps.
- Adult content filter for every browser and app on the PC, with SafeSearch locked and a cool-down before it can be turned off.
- One switch to block YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and Facebook Reels without blocking the whole site.
- Schedules, breaks, daily allowances, Lock this PC for a set time, and an option to block Task Manager during a session.
- With the Timer lock, a session can't be stopped early: Stop is refused, and closing Halt, restarting, changing the clock, uninstalling, Task Manager (blocked in Pro) or deleting the block (the service puts it back within a minute) all leave it in place. Only the PC's administrator, through Safe Mode, can undo it, which no Windows app can prevent; we keep that so a bug can never lock someone out. With a standard Windows account and the administrator password held by someone else, nobody at the keyboard can end a session early.

## Plans

- Halt Basic: free for good. Up to 10 websites (or parts of them), the Timer lock, one-tap bundles, stats and a weekly challenge.
- Halt Pro: $29 once, on all your PCs, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. You unlock it in the app with the email you paid with (a 6-digit code is emailed); there is no key to keep. Everything above, yours for good, with every future update included. Every install starts with 7 days of Halt Pro, free, with no card and no account.

What other blockers charge (checked 19 October 2026 on freedom.to, covenanteyes.com and Apple's App Store): Freedom $8.99 a month or $99.50 for life; BlockerX $139.99 a year or $149.99 for life; Covenant Eyes $18 a month or $950 for life. Halt Pro is $29 once, with no subscription option at all.

## Installing, and what Halt changes on a PC

- Requirements: Windows 10 or 11 on a 64-bit (x64) PC. The installer is code-signed by its verified publisher.
- Install: open Halt-Setup.exe and follow the steps. The first page lists what Halt changes, and installing continues only after ticking "I understand". Halt then opens by itself: add the sites and apps to block, pick a lock and press Start.
- New apps get a warning until enough people have installed them. In Edge: the three dots next to the download, Keep, Show more, Keep anyway. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC": More info, then Run anyway (it shows Halt's verified publisher).
- While a focus session runs, Chrome, Edge, Brave and Firefox block the list through their own policy settings, so they show "managed by your organization". Nothing is blocked until the person chooses what to block.
- A small Windows service keeps a running session's blocks in place, also after a restart.
- Halt's browser extension is added only if the person agrees to it in the app.
- Only if turned on: the adult filter changes the DNS, and the Task Manager guard turns off Task Manager during a session.
- Halt can't be uninstalled while a session runs or the adult filter is on. Any other time, Settings > Apps removes it completely and puts everything back.
- Already bought Halt Pro: in Settings, press "I already bought it" and enter the email used to pay.

## Privacy

No account, no ads, no tracking. Block lists, stats and settings stay on the PC. Halt Pro checks its license with our server about once a day. The website counts visits as daily totals, without cookies or anything that identifies a visitor.

## Limits

- Windows only for now. Halt for Mac and apps for Android and iPhone are coming soon.
- On sites that change pages without reloading, such as YouTube, a rule for one page may not catch moves inside the site; a daily limit is the surer way to cut down there.
